newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran's leader warns U.S. against attacking.
newsitem.headline: Iran's leader warns U.S. against attacking.

text.p: Iranian supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on Friday warned the United States against attacking Iran, saying such an assault would only increase the hostility of its people towards Washington and its allies.

"They (U.S.) have spread (rumours) across the world that America will carry out a military attack. I do not believe it. Of course it is possible. We will stand up to anything and the Iranian people is afraid of nothing," Khamenei said in a mass Friday prayer sermon broadcast on Tehran radio.

"Assuming there is expedient thinking (in Washington), then they should realise that such an act would be against America's interests and would benefit the revolution," Khamenei told worshippers on the first of ten days of celebrations marking the anniversary of Iran's 1979 Islamic revolution.

"America and the Zionists primarily want to break away the people from the revolution...but that (attack) would only make this nation more steadfast and increase its enmity towards America and the Zionists," Khamenei added.
The large crowd, gathered at Tehran University, responded by chanting "Death to America" and "Death to Israel".

Iranian officials have reacted strongly to Western media reports linking Tehran to a June bombing in Saudi Arabia that killed 19 U.S. airmen, saying the reports indicated Washington was preparing an attack on the Islamic republic.
"If anyone believes that it is possible through threats to force this country's officials to change their positions, then they are badly mistaken," Khamenei said.
Iran has not been officially linked to the truck bomb attack and the country has denied any involvement.

Tehran radio said thousands of people held a funeral procession after the prayers for 1,000 Iranians killed in the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war and whose remains have been found recently in the former battlefields.
